slides.title: Nyl12–PA6: mechanism and redesign
slides.takeaway: Research progress and decision briefing | 23 November 2026
bullets: Goal: identify credible catalytic states and design more active Nyl 12 variants.
Scope: PA6 force field → MD ensembles → QM/MM paths → sequence design.
Key distinction: completed calculations, accepted geometry and mechanistic validation are separate.
Working conclusions; unpublished experimental context is identified explicitly.
slides.notes: Working interpretation; source records are authoritative. Process completion does not establish scientific acceptance.

slides.title: What we can conclude today
slides.takeaway: A useful computational foundation; a viable mechanism is still unresolved.

slides.title: Scientific objective and success criteria
slides.takeaway: Mechanism and engineering are linked, separately testable deliverables.
bullets: Mechanism: chemically consistent E–S→acylenzyme pathway with a credible barrier and independently verified TS connectivity.
Engineering: symmetry-aware designs that preserve maturation, assembly, substrate access and productive configurations.
A stable, discrete TI1 minimum is not a prerequisite for hydrolysis.
Long-polymer binding, chemistry and product release can limit activity differently.
slides.notes: Working interpretation; source records are authoritative. Process completion does not establish scientific acceptance.

slides.title: Experimental baseline: two distinct assay contexts
slides.takeaway: Endpoint conversion does not uniquely determine kcat or a chemical barrier.
rows: Active enzyme concentration and temperature-adjusted pH uncertain
Polymer powder; product profiles rather than a defined elementary rate
L4→two L2 is a modeling hypothesis; long polymer is likely
Treat activity labels and figure/workbook linkage as provisional
slides.caption: Published Drufva work primarily reported linear PA6 trimer; no experimentally established L4→L2 precursor–product relationship.

slides.title: Structure, assembly and residue identities
slides.takeaway: Catalytic Thr233 is Amber Thr929; neighboring Thr234 is Amber Thr930.
bullets: Nyl 12 matures by autocatalytic cleavage; substrate hydrolysis must be distinguished from maturation chemistry.
The working model retains the tetramer and four active sites; designs use explicit sequence-symmetry ties.
n 12c.cif is a supplied, edited tetramer derivative of 9Z0B; 9Z0A is a complementary room-temperature structure.
Phe113 and Asn186 are candidate oxyanion-hole donors; Asp272/Asp274 and the Thr N-terminus form the acid–base environment.

slides.title: Mechanistic hypotheses and observables
slides.takeaway: Track complete proton inventories rather than a prescribed proton label.

cards.title: Direct acylation
cards.text:
OG1 attacks the amide carbonyl as a proton reaches the leaving N.
A four-membered pseudo-ring route was tested.

cards.title: N-terminal relay
cards.text:
Thr N accepts an OG1 proton, then can donate a proton onward.
N-H identity may exchange without invalidating chemistry.

cards.title: Assisted networks
cards.text:
Asp and water networks may reorganize proton delivery.
Require actual geometry and a distinct, testable role.

slides.title: Computational workflow and safeguards
slides.takeaway: Reproducibility and scientific acceptance are explicit at every stage.
bullets: Boltz/AF3 or experimental structure → chemistry/atom-map audit → solvated MM preparation and independent MD.
Snapshot selection → MM minimization → DFTB3/MM E–S optimization → coordinate driving or NEB.
Separate TS force convergence, Hessian index and downhill connectivity; use US/MBAR for sampled free energies.
Scripts, immutable source snapshots, input hashes, environments, tmux logs and process/scientific receipts are retained.
slides.notes: Working interpretation; source records are authoritative. Process completion does not establish scientific acceptance.

slides.title: PA6 parameters: reusable modular architecture
slides.takeaway: Methods and limitations transfer from the separate polyamide-amber-ff project.
bullets: Amber ff19SB protein, TIP3P water and GAFF2/RESP PA6 substrate parameters support current MD comparisons.
Modular residues: P6N (+1), repeated P6I (0) and P6C (−1), with explicit polymer connectivity and atom mapping.
QM electrostatics and torsional validation address limitations of the original AM1-BCC/GAFF model.
Current release is MD-ready for zwitterionic PA6 L4 only; compact-conformer electrostatics and extension to other chemistries remain open.
slides.notes: Current release README/manifest supersedes historical October31 presentation holds. Three 500ps validationreplicas and all8 declaredbondedprofilegates passed. Scope is P6N–P6I–P6I–P6C; does not certify arbitrarylengths, bulknylon, TI1 or acylenzyme. Existing FFdeck was consulted; current manuscriptfigures are integrated directly.

slides.title: Parameterization validation: what matters
slides.takeaway: A parameter release is evaluated across chemistry, electrostatics and conformational behavior.
bullets: RESP: charge conservation, equivalent-atom constraints, transferability of the internal residue and ESP quality.
Bonded terms: QM/MM torsional profiles, amide planarity, forward/reverse scans and consistent solvent protocols.
System behavior: topology round trips, unrestrained relaxation and independent MD stability.
Compare AM1-BCC/GAFF, integrated RESP/GAFF2 and modular RESP/GAFF2 under matched conditions; binding persistence alone is insufficient.
slides.notes: Working interpretation; source records are authoritative. Process completion does not establish scientific acceptance.

slides.takeaway: All deposited comparison sites pass the unchanged structural gate.

slides.title: MCCE and crystal contacts: uncertainty remains
slides.takeaway: Successful execution is not validation of a pKa prediction.
bullets: Negoro’s protonated-Asp assignment is a mechanistic inference; mutational effects are partly confounded by maturation.
Across 31 deposited NylC sites, minimum Asp–Asp O···O distances were3.58–4.17 Å; none was below3.5 Å.
Repaired 5XYG / 7YU0 / 7YU1 MCCE runs completed, but target curves/bounds and poor fits remain unqualified.
Mature 5XYG labels Asp306/Asp308<0 and N-terminal Thr>14 are not accepted protonation evidence. Compare matched-input curves and parameters.
slides.notes: Current reruns native_completed_pka_unqualified. Sampling_convergencefalse; assigned_statesfalse. Known proline FTPL/legacy charge-template inconsistency, protein-only pilot, six MC runs x2000 iterations. Precursor group fits can be broad/non-sigmoidal; out-of-grid labels are bounds.

slides.title: HG1 ownership in the completed biased data
slides.takeaway: N-terminal binding supports a relay hypothesis, not established transfer order.
slides.caption: Counts are neither equilibrium populations nor bond classifications. Concatenated windows are not a continuous reaction movie.
slides.notes: Old direct-PT umbrellas already sampled N-boundHG1. The mechanistically useful question is coupling proton occupancy to attack/acylation. HG1→Nalpha followed by H1/H2→leavingN can be a valid relay; restoring OG1OH/NalphaNH2 invalidates an intended alkoxide/ammonium state.

slides.title: Current test: unbiased relay-state relaxations
slides.takeaway: Relay seed w033: force accepted; full Hessian ongoing, minimum not yet certified.
slides.caption: All three have actual Nalpha–HG1 bonds, with H1/H2 retained on Nalpha. No reaction-coordinate or positional potentials in the movable region.
slides.notes: w033 force acceptance is distinct from stationary-point classification. The full Hessian is ongoing; no minimum is certified. The three configurations preserve the declared N-terminal proton inventory and fixed exterior; no live host or GPU availability is implied.

slides.title: How the two mutable masks were chosen
slides.takeaway: Focused 19 positions are retained; broader 29 adds ten audited alpha sites.
bullets: Focused beta: local 39, 41 = canonical precursor 271, 273. These 19 sites form the unchanged base mask.
New sites: RSA ≥ 0.25 in every copy of both WT parents; no other-chain heavy contact ≤ 4 Å.
slides.notes: The focused mask is retained unchanged, not retrospectively subjected to the broader-addition gate. Four additions are in the 6–12 Å shell and six in the 12–16 Å shell. RSA uses Tien 2013 normalization. Parent structures were WT seed 02 and seed 03.

slides.title: Selected mutations: canonical precursor numbering
slides.takeaway: Full substitution lists; beta local L39F is canonical L271F.
bullets: mask_03 (focused): S50A, V51A, S153A, A187T, V188I, L271F.
mask_07 (broader): S50A, V51A, A92K, N97D, S153T, A187T, V188T.
Equivalent alpha chains A–D share one sequence; beta chains E–H share one sequence.
Catalytic/maturation protections remain fixed: alpha 113, 156, 186, 222–232; beta local 1–3, 40, 42 (canonical 233–235, 272, 274).
slides.notes: Canonical precursor numbering covers alpha residues 1–232 and beta residues 233–328; beta local index is canonical minus 232. Mutation lists describe whole precursor sequences, not individual site substitutions per tetramer.

slides.title: Why test the flipped PA6 pose?
slides.takeaway: Signed φ identifies orientation; it does not establish relay competence.
bullets: Flipped-only MD tests the N-terminal relay hypothesis; it does not assume the relay is already positioned.
WT negative φ: Nα–leaving N mean 4.65 Å (4.24–5.47; n=16). Positive φ: 3.61 Å (3.51–3.67; n=4).
Current negative-φ poses require reorganization or a water relay; the shorter positive-φ distance alone also proves nothing.
Proton-transfer direction remains unresolved. Selected starts and finite unrestrained MD cannot establish unbiased binding preference.
slides.notes: The negative signed projected phi denotes flipped orientation only under the consistent scissile-amide mapping. Lead audit of relaxed WT sites: negative n=16, mean 4.65 Å, range 4.24–5.47 Å; positive n=4, mean 3.61 Å, range 3.51–3.67 Å. Selected WT seed04 4.59–4.87 Å, mask_03 4.30–5.19 Å, mask_07 4.30–4.89 Å, V111C 5.26–5.45 Å. Geometric proximity alone establishes neither transfer direction nor relay competence. The PI-selected campaign remains flipped-only.

slides.title: Design interpretation and experimental spending
slides.takeaway: Current scores do not provide compelling evidence of improved catalytic activity.
bullets: Broader mask_07 has 6 joint sites across3/5 predictions; focused mask_03 provides a comparison with fewer substitutions.
Known-active K59D has0/20 joint passes and V111C 7/20: activity calibration remains a major limitation.
Four sites per model and prediction seeds are correlated; do not interpret site fractions as hit probabilities.
Calibrate controls and matched starting ensembles before a bounded variantMD follow-up or experimental nomination.
slides.notes: Working interpretation; source records are authoritative. Process completion does not establish scientific acceptance.

slides.title: Engineering precedent: Puetz KnowVolution
slides.takeaway: Empirical anchoring and productive binding can guide improvement before full mechanism resolution.
bullets: NylC F134W/D304M/R330A improved PA6 specific activity6.9-fold in the reported parent background.
Adding D99R reduced that improvement to3.9-fold: negative epistasis matters.
Persistent contacts to a charged oligomer terminus were associated with poorer performance in the combined variant.
ForNyl 12: consider terminal artifacts, access and release alongside catalytic geometry; validate mutation combinations experimentally.
slides.notes: Puetzetal.,ChemSusChem2025,18,e202500257. Mutagenesis/MD/recombination study; this does not validate ouractivityranker. Homologmutationnumbersmustbemappedbeforetransfer.

slides.title: Mechanism-agent and resource strategy
slides.takeaway: Tool-backed bounded tasks; human control of chemistry and expensive launches.
bullets: GPT-OSS and Mistral pilots both made consequential chemistry errors; neither qualified for autonomous scientific dispatch.
Next tool task: matched-inputMCCE/PROPKA curve audit with explicit preparation and parameter checks.
MuseGlimmer 30B is the intended alternative model; a held-out qualification would be a separate, bounded test.
Maintain one roadmap, compact decision packets and existing source-linked evidence. Keep model servers off between requests.
slides.notes: Working interpretation; source records are authoritative. Process completion does not establish scientific acceptance.

slides.takeaway: Concentrate effort on calculations that distinguish mechanistic hypotheses.
